cases.question: does Atlas claim anything inside verus! blocks?
cases.answer: no edge and no function: 0 of the about 5,170 fn declarations written inside 451 verus! blocks are censused, and no INVOKES or DISPATCHES_TO touches a block -- but FUNCTION_IDENTITY, SYMBOL, TYPE and FUNCTION_SIGNATURE coverage said OBSERVED on all 297 files holding one: the falsification

falsification.claim: declaration coverage OBSERVED (exhaustive) on files whose declarations are written inside macros Atlas does not expand
falsification.evidence: 297 verus files with verus! blocks (3,019 fn declarations in vstd alone) claimed FUNCTION_IDENTITY, SYMBOL, TYPE and FUNCTION_SIGNATURE OBSERVED with 0 functions recorded inside the blocks; the same over-claim held on Atlas's own census (the enums written in vocabulary_enum!, the structs of typed_id!, closures written inside matches! and inside local templates) and, found while fixing, a written source module (core/src/coverage) dropped as generated output, unions unrecorded, and items in const and static initializers unrecorded

implementation.mechanism_vs_implementation: nothing absorbed: the verifier's mechanism stays behind the oracle boundary; the fix is Atlas's own honesty about what its syntactic walk cannot see
implementation.change: ADR 0096: a place the walk cannot see into -- an unexpanded macro invocation, an unparsed item, a block the walk never enters (initializers, discriminants, expressions inside types), a same-file macro_rules! template reached through a fixpoint of its invocations, a closure or async block written in an unexpanded macro inside a body -- that spells a declaration holds SYMBOL and TYPE (and FUNCTION_IDENTITY and FUNCTION_SIGNATURE when it spells fn or a closure) UNKNOWN with a named INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS diagnostic and GAP-HIDDEN-DECLARATION; unions, foreign types and trait aliases are recorded; an output-named directory is source when its files show a Rust module or package (file presence only)
implementation.falsification: the first measurement's over-claim, then two independent review rounds: a stack overflow and a quadratic scan in a directory parser (replaced by a rule that reads no file contents), initializer items, local and chained templates, crate-root module resolution; 55 of 55 final mutants killed
implementation.review: two independent adversarial reviews and a verification of the last round's fixes
